newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - GUS buys U.S. firm for $1.7 billion.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - GUS buys U.S. firm for $1.7 billion.

text.p: Great Universal Stores Plc (GUS) said on Thursday that it was merging its information services business CCN with U.S. firm Experian in a deal that is costing the British retailer $1.7 billion.

GUS's payment for the credit, marketing and real estate information services company based in Orange County, California, will be financed through an $800 million loan with the rest coming from its own resources.
"If GUS had not bought Experian, then Experian would have liked to have bought CCN, because the natural fit of the two companies is quite outstanding," GUS chairman Lord Wolfson said.
The deal was well received by the London equity market with GUS shares storming ahead 42p to 632-1/2 during the morning. The stock reached a year's low of 583p on November 8.

"They seem to be paying a fairly full price in terms of Experian's earnings and sales, but the deal seems to have a certain amount of commercial logic," said William Cullum, an analyst at Paribas Capital Markets.

GUS said the acquisition of Experian would significantly expand its presence in the information services market and it expects the merger to enhance earnings in the first year as well as generate strong cash flow.

Wolfson said that CCN and Experian has been talking to each other for several years, but stated, "it really matured into serious conversations in the summer of this year and it has taken a few months to reach full agreement."
He estimated that the combined business would make up around 15 to 20 percent of the entire GUS group ... "in other words it is a major core division."

GUS, whose businesses include Burberry's and Scotch House as well as four mail order catalogue units, set up CCN in 1980 to satisfy demand from banks, retailers and other lenders for credit information on their customers.
"CCN has grown steadily but particularly dramatically over the last four or five years," Wolfson told Reuters.
"It's grown from originally serving our home shopping division to become a business in its own right and with this (merger) it will become a global leader."
Experian has three proprietary databases -- consumers, businesses and real estate -- with information on over 190 million people and 91 million households in the U.S.

Once part of TRW Inc, an 80.4 percent stake in Experian was acquired in February this year by a Bain Capital Inc unit, Thomas H Lee Co, and other investors. Experian generated sales of $540 million in 1995 and a pro forma profit of $109 million.
GUS said that the two operations were well placed to develop new business opportunities and, in particular, to provide global solutions to large multinational clients.
